slices.name: ws16-p2-01-the-letters-rules-and-its-cleaner
slices.brief: Checkpoint P's first step: the rules of a newsletter letter, written once for the page and the server, and the cleaner every saved letter passes through. Two new files that nothing imports yet, so the step can be built in the free days before K's switch-on day without touching a file that the five-spot fix or WS16 steps 9 to 11 change. It adds no switch and no migration. What it leaves unchanged: everything. Nothing imports either file, so every page, every email and the worker's bundle are byte for byte as on main. Built on the branch redesign/ws16-page, cut from main, in its own working copy. About six files; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. 1. domain/mail/letter.ts (new, pure, no import outside domain/): letterParts(html) reads the h2 headings of a cleaned letter in order and answers [{ title, name }]; a name is the heading's words in lower case with letters and digits kept and every other run turned into one hyphen, and a second heading with the same words gets "-2", a third "-3"; a heading with no words is skipped. withAnchors(html, parts) writes an empty named anchor just before each part's heading (), the form part one's build notes ask for, since a target with only an id fails in Gmail and classic Outlook. STARTERS: 'blank' (the month's band and an empty page), 'monthly' ("Monthly newsletter": A note from the president, Coming up, Results, From the clubs, Scholastic, Board business, in that order), 'results-and-thanks' and 'short-notice', each holding headings only, and the prompts of the empty parts as the board words them ("Write your opening here", "Add what is coming up", "Add results or club news"). defaultSubject(month) answers "LCA Newsletter · December 2026" for December 2026. LETTER_MAX_BYTES = 80000. 2. functions/utils/mail/letterClean.ts (new): export async function cleanLetterHtml(html), which answers the cleaned letter, or null for a letter it cannot make clean. It uses the method of sanitizePostHtml in functions/utils/posts.ts (the Workers runtime's HTML rewriter with an allow list), narrowed to what the editor makes and with that method's blind spot closed. Kept: p, br, strong, em, h2, h3, ul, ol, li, hr and a. Every attribute is removed. A link keeps its href only when it starts with https://, http:// or mailto: and holds no quote mark, angle bracket, backtick, space or control character; any other link loses its tag and keeps its words; a site path is refused, since an email has no page to be relative to. Removed with everything they hold: script, style, iframe, object, embed, img, svg and math, and the tags whose inside the rewriter hands on as raw text: textarea, title, noscript, xmp, noembed, noframes, plaintext and template. That second group is the blind spot: sanitizePostHtml removes only script, style, iframe, object and embed with what they hold and unwraps every other tag that is not on its list (functions/utils/posts.ts lines 68 to 75), so would leave a live img behind once the textarea's own tags are gone. Any other tag is removed and its words kept; comments are removed. Last, the cleaner cleans its own result once more and answers it only when that second pass changes nothing; otherwise it answers null and the caller refuses the letter in words. So a saved letter is always one the cleaner would leave alone. 3. Tests. test/unit/mail-letter.test.ts (new): the parts and their names, two same headings, an empty heading, the anchors, the six headings in order, the default subject, and that every sample word in the file is plainly made up (decision 39). test/integration/mail-letter-clean.test.ts (new, in the integration suite because that suite runs inside the Workers runtime): script, style, img, iframe, onclick, a javascript: link, a data: link, a comment and broken markup are gone or made safe; one case for each of textarea, title, noscript, xmp, noembed, noframes, plaintext, template, svg and math, each holding an img with an onerror and a link with an onclick, and nothing of either is left; a single-quoted link that holds a double quote (href='https://x" onclick="y') comes out with no onclick and no href; the allowed tags come out as they went in; cleaning twice changes nothing; a result the second pass would change is answered as null; a letter over LETTER_MAX_BYTES is the caller's to refuse, not the cleaner's. The scout also runs the same inputs once through sanitizePostHtml, in the same runtime and without changing it, and the record states what it lets through: mending the News posts' cleaner is a small change of its own, put to K, and not part of this half. 4. The record: the page half's part of REDESIGN_STATUS.md is opened in WS16 part two step 3, with the switch. This step's block is written then, from the notes kept here. Covers the design scout's P7 (the usual six headings; the list made from the headings and not typed).

slices.brief:
Checkpoint P's second step: the email's navy look, the LCA president's pick (decision 53), board Newsletter-Email-6, "The navy band, with In this issue". One pure function in domain/, so the server sends with it and the page's side preview draws with it, and one image. functions/utils/emailLayout.ts is not edited. It adds no switch and no migration. slices.name: ws16-p2-03-the-letters-storage-and-saving
slices.brief:
Checkpoint P's third step: where a letter lives while it is written, and the page half's switch. Migration 0061 adds one table; four endpoint methods read, save, start and list letters; mailPage with MAIL_PAGE_ON is the pair the whole page ships under. What it leaves unchanged with the switch off: the four methods answer 404 and read nothing, the new table is empty, and nothing a visitor or a member meets changes; the newsletter tab, its endpoints and every email are as on main. This step may be built before K's switch-on day. It adds lines to files WS16 steps 9 to 11 also add lines to (the two switch files and their tests, the contracts' registry and index, src/areas/admin/api.ts and its fixture); the page branch is rebased once onto main after checkpoint N has merged, and the live figures below are measured again then. It does not touch src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx, src/pages/AdminPage.tsx, functions/utils/mail/lists.ts or functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts. About twenty-three files, most of them one-line pins.

1. functions/db/schema.ts and migrations/0061_newsletter_issues.sql (new, written by npm run db:generate and staged under drizzle/ with its snapshot and journal): one table, newsletter_issues: id, list_id, month_label, subject, preheader, body_html, version (starting at 1), created_by, created_at, updated_by, updated_at, campaign_id (set when the letter is sent), set_aside_at (set when a new letter replaces it), tested_at (set when a test of the letter as it stands has gone, and emptied by the next save that changes it; WS16 part two step 6 reads it for K's choice 4), and the columns checkpoint Q reads, which stay empty until then, so Q carries no migration: send_at, scheduled_by, scheduled_at, link_check, held_reason, pinned_at, pinned_name. One unique index: one open letter for a list (campaign_id IS NULL AND set_aside_at IS NULL). No CHECK is written, no table is rebuilt and no other table changes. A letter's state is read from these columns and never stored as a status.

slices.name: ws16-p2-04-the-page-writing-and-the-side-preview
slices.brief:
Checkpoint P's fourth step: the approved page itself, Newsletter-Page-4 as it stands after round 15 (decision 51), for writing: the head, From and Subject, the tools, the letter you click and type on, saving by itself, and the side preview, on a computer, a tablet and a phone. The bar's contents come in WS16 part two step 5 and sending in step 6. Large; the build may split it in two, the computer first, then tablet and phone. What it leaves unchanged with the switch off: the route is not registered, so /admin/newsletter leads where it leads today (Admin's own redirect); no link leads to the page; test/a11y/baseline.json is unchanged; no other page changes. With the switch on and before step 6, the page is reached by its address alone. It may be started before K's switch-on day; it is parked at its last green commit on K's days. It does not touch src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx or src/pages/AdminPage.tsx. About nineteen files.

1. src/App.tsx: a lazy AdminNewsletterPage and, only with FEATURES.mailPage, the route /admin/newsletter inside RoleProtectedRoute with roles={ADMIN_PANEL_ROLES}, fallbackToToolsHome and allowMediaManager, as /admin/:section has. test/unit/app-routes.test.tsx's count of lazy pages moves 35 to 36.

The page lets in whoever the server lets send: the LCA admins, the president, and the media manager on the route's own answer; an officer without the seat is sent to Admin. An officer who holds the seat sees no "View only" badge here.
3. The head (P1): the crumb "Admin / Newsletter", the title, the month with the letter's state in words (Draft, and the states of step 6 and checkpoint Q later), the saved line, and Help and "Admin sections" at the right. The saved line's states, in words beside any colour: "Saving", "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM", "Could not save" with "Try again", and "Player Two changed this letter at 2:17 PM" with "Show their letter" when a save is refused for an old version.

Subject is a field with its pencil mark, an outline and a count ("30 of 60 letters") when clicked; the count is a guide and the server's limit stays 200.
5. The tools (P5): Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link and Undo, and the Add menu, which the approved board names "Add a photo, event or line". By K's choice 5 as recommended it reads "Add an event or line" in checkpoint P: it holds a line here, the event form joins it in WS16 part two step 5, and the photo joins it, with the board's own name, in step 12. Each at least 44px.

slices.brief:
Checkpoint Q's first step: the server side of "Send later" (decision 51, board Newsletter-Page-4-Schedule): a letter can be given a day and a time in Central time, the time can be changed or cleared, and a phase of the worker's five-minute run sends the letter when the time comes. No migration: the columns came with 0061. No new status, no new cron and no change to the campaign tables. What it leaves unchanged with the switch off: the two new methods answer 404; the worker's phase returns at its first line and reads nothing, so each five-minute run makes the same queries as today; a save is today's, since no letter holds a time; the page shows no arrow on Send; the audit log's new labels are never written. Built on checkpoint P's head, after checkpoint N has merged, while P waits for K's word; checkpoint Q opens once P has merged. About twenty-one files.

2. domain/mail/sendLater.ts (new, pure): toInstant(day, time) turns a Central day and time into an instant with lcaTimeToMs (domain/format/centralTime.ts) and reads it back: a time that does not exist (2:00 AM to 2:59 AM on Sunday, March 14, 2027) is refused; a time that comes twice (1:00 AM to 1:59 AM on Sunday, November 7, 2027) means the first; a past day or time is refused. LATE_AFTER_MS, the limit of K's choice 8 (6 hours as recommended). The words for the head: "Scheduled for Tuesday, December 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM" through the site's own date and time formatters, "Sending now" from the letter's time until a run has picked it up, and "Changed since the last test".
3. The version rule. Every write to a letter's schedule moves its version by one, as a save does: setting a time, changing it, clearing it ("Do not send it"), and the worker's own write when it holds a letter. So whatever read the letter before such a write holds an old version and is refused. The test's mark alone does not move it.
4. functions/api/admin/mail/newsletter/issue/schedule.ts (new): POST { version, day, time } sets or changes the time, behind requireListMailer and 404 unless MAIL_LATER_ON. It refuses, with "Send a test of this letter first", a letter with no test of its present words (K's choice 4 as recommended). It writes send_at (an instant in UTC, in the form the table's other times use, so two compare as text), scheduled_by, scheduled_at and link_check, the 16 characters of the site's link key at that moment (linkKeyCheck), clears held_reason, moves the version, and answers 409 on an old version; 503 without the link key. DELETE { version } is "Do not send it": it empties send_at and moves the version, the letter is a draft again and nothing is deleted. "Send now" is the page's own send of step 6, whose batch also empties the time.
5. Saving a scheduled letter (functions/utils/mail/issues.ts): saveIssue's WHERE gains "send_at is empty or still to come", against the server's clock. Until its time a scheduled letter is saved like any other and can be tested (decision 51). From its time on a save is refused in words ("This newsletter is sending now"), so what goes out is the letter as it stood at its time, whichever five-minute run picks it up, and no run can lose a race with a save. To write on it again a person chooses "Change the day or time" or "Do not send it".
6. functions/utils/mail/later.ts (new): sendDueLetter(env). It returns at once unless MAIL_LATER_ON. One query reads the one open letter whose send_at has come, with its version. Then, in this order. Later than LATE_AFTER_MS: the letter goes back to a draft with held_reason in words ("Not sent: more than 6 hours late"), by one write that requires the version just read and a time still set, so it never overwrites a time a person has changed in between, and one activity row is written in the scheduler's name. The scheduler may no longer send: the phase reads the scheduler's member row, which the activity row needs in any case, and holds the letter the same way, with "Not sent: the person who scheduled it may no longer send the newsletter", unless that person is still an LCA admin, the president or a holder of the Media manager seat now (holdsMediaManagerSeat in functions/utils/admin/mediaManager.ts, a file that imports nothing, so the worker's closure gains no package). A second factor belongs to a signed-in session and cannot be checked from the worker; the record says so. While Resend sends, or without the link key: nothing is written and the next run tries again. Otherwise createListCampaign with the letter { id, version } as read, its stored link_check, and due set: the campaign's insert then also requires, in the same statement, that the letter still holds a time and that the time has come (send_at IS NOT NULL AND send_at <= now), beside open, unsent and at that version. A "Do not send it" or a new time that lands between the phase's read and its batch has moved the version, so the insert makes nothing and nothing is sent. The phase's send does not ask for tested_at: by decision 51 a scheduled letter goes as it stands at its time (K's choice 4 (b) would add that condition and hold the letter). If another newsletter is still sending, createListCampaign answers null and the next run tries again. When it makes the campaign: one activity row, today's group_email_sent with detail { by: 'schedule', scheduled_by, last_saved_by, month }, in the scheduler's name, and the sweep in the same run starts the sending. People are counted at that moment (S7).
7. workers/daily-emails/src/index.ts: in the five-minute branch of scheduled(), before the sweep, await phase('newsletter send later', () => sendDueLetter(env)); the sweep's phase follows as today.

Each is computed at the read.

So the page's steps 1 to 5 are built in those free days, on their own branch, redesign/ws16-page, in their own working copy. Throwing nothing off: nothing of the page half merges into main until the switch-on change, the cutover change and checkpoint N have merged and the first newsletter has finished sending; on K's days, and while checkpoint N's steps, its merge-safety review or its fix round are under way, no page step is started and one under way is parked at its last green commit; checkpoint N starts on its day from main whatever the page's state; four files (src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx, src/pages/AdminPage.tsx, functions/utils/mail/lists.ts and functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts) are not touched by the page branch until checkpoint N has merged, since N's steps change three of them and a checkpoint's fix round changed the fourth in checkpoint M; the page branch is then rebased once onto main at N's merge commit, at its own cost; checkpoint O keeps its day, and its one step is scouted again on main after checkpoint Q has merged.
